claims.text: US President Donald Trump met top artificial intelligence executives at the White House on Tuesday.
US President Donald Trump announced that leading AI companies agreed to a framework to self-police the development of artificial intelligence technology.
US President Donald Trump stated that he would officially rename artificial intelligence technology to 'super intelligence'.
US President Donald Trump said of AI technology, 'I will never stifle the growth of a technology that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution.'
The White House Accord on Super Intelligence was signed by representatives from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, NVIDIA, and xAI.
House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that the White House Accord on Super Intelligence is entirely voluntary.
Google CEO Sundar Pichai stated on X that Google has invested hundreds of billions of dollars over the past two years across its AI stack.
The White House Accord on Super Intelligence outlines a four-layer framework of controls and audits for frontier AI systems.
OpenAI scrapped the release of its flagship AI model GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns.
A Marist Poll found that 65% of registered US voters opposed data centres being built in their local areas.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated at the White House summit that AI technology 'has very real risks'.
US military forces completed their withdrawal from their remaining bases in Iraq on Wednesday.
The US troop withdrawal from Iraq was agreed upon in 2024 under US President Joe Biden.
A total of 4,500 American military personnel died in Iraq over more than 20 years of war.
Iraq declared four national 'Sovereignty Days' public holidays to mark the complete withdrawal of US military forces.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi set a revised target deadline of June 2027 to disarm all non-state militias in Iraq.
Remaining US military personnel in Iraq had consolidated at an airbase in Erbil in late 2025.
Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, called the US military departure a 'historic victory'.
Senior security official Colonel Khalid al-Bayati stated that a suspected Islamic State cell in Kirkuk was preparing suicide attacks to coincide with the US departure.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi declared in a statement that October 1 would mark a new day for Iraq free of any foreign military presence.
The withdrawal of US troops from Iraq includes the departure of personnel and removal of US air defense systems from Erbil.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that more than 440 people, mostly minors, were detained during nationwide student protests.
The French government's draft 2027 budget includes a planned €54 billion spending savings drive.
The French Education Ministry reported that around 400 schools out of 3,700 nationwide were affected by student disruptions.
Unions estimated that approximately 300,000 public sector workers participated in strike action across France.
Sophie Binet, general secretary of the CGT union, gave the French government 48 hours to reverse planned budget cuts before deciding on further strike action.
Officials reported that 48 law enforcement officers were injured during nationwide clashes on Tuesday.
Ryad Rani, president of the Union Syndicale Lycéenne, called for a total blockade of French high schools while urging peaceful protests.
French Education Minister Édouard Geffray wrote on X that student protest violence was 'indefensible'.
King Mohammed VI of Morocco appointed Marrakesh's mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister.
Fatima Zahra El Mansouri's Authenticity and Modernity Party won 97 seats in Morocco's 395-member parliament.
Fatima Zahra El Mansouri is the second woman to lead a government in the Arab world, after Tunisia's Najla Bouden.
The Islamist Justice and Development Party secured 54 seats in Morocco's parliamentary election.
The Authenticity and Modernity Party pledged to achieve average annual economic growth of five percent during its five-year term.
Former Prime Minister Abdelilah Benkirane of the Justice and Development Party ruled out joining a coalition government led by the Authenticity and Modernity Party.
The US Supreme Court granted an emergency request allowing the Trump administration to resume deporting migrants to third countries without offering pre-removal safety hearings.
Human rights groups estimate that more than 25,000 people have been deported to 29 third countries under the US policy implemented last year.
US Supreme Court Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan, and Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented from the emergency order.
The US Supreme Court agreed to hear full oral arguments regarding the legality of third-country deportations in December.
US Solicitor General John Sauer told the court that rapid third-country deportation is an essential tool to remove certain non-citizens.
Burundi signed an agreement with the US to accept third-country non-citizen deportees who do not face criminal prosecution or links to terrorism.
UK counter-terrorism police arrested five British men from London in the Gloucestershire countryside near RAF Fairford.
Police found several barrels in white vans seized near RAF Fairford, one containing petrol and others empty, but no improvised explosive devices.
Eighty-five households in Whelford were evacuated following the security alert near RAF Fairford.
US President Donald Trump said of the release of the Fairford suspects, 'I'm surprised that they released them. I wouldn't have done that.'
The Iranian Embassy in London stated that it categorically rejects and strongly condemns speculation linking Iran to the RAF Fairford incident.
Head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing Laurence Taylor defended the decision to bail the five suspects, calling it an investigative decision grounded in policing powers.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated in a Fox News interview that the security incident near RAF Fairford clearly involved the hand of a foreign actor.
Ukrainian Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko stated that air raid alerts cost Ukraine an estimated $45 million for every hour business is brought to a halt.
Oleksandr Kravchenko reported that Russian strikes in 2026 caused an estimated $10 billion in damage to fixed assets in Ukraine.
The Ukrainian government introduced a two-tier air warning system, using 'red' alerts for missile threats and 'yellow' alerts for drone threats.
Ukraine narrowed its remaining budget shortfall for 2026 from $27 billion down to $20 billion through spending cuts and domestic reserves.
The Zaporizhstal steel plant in Zaporizhzhia shut down indefinitely following four waves of Russian missile strikes in August and September.
Russian missile strikes on the Zaporizhstal steel plant killed eight workers and wounded 31 others.
ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih announced on September 25 that it was unable to reopen following five weeks of repeated Russian attacks.
A Russian drone strike hit Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences building in central Kyiv, killing one person and injuring three others.
